title: Finite matrix models for reductions of integral constant local modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be any scheme, with a fixed small skeleton of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $A_n=A/\ell^n$, $B_n=\underline{A_n}$ and $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}B_n$, with their canonical coefficient maps [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use sheaves of modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and derived scalar extension computed by K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $L$ be a $B$-module sheaf with a finite constant local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a pro-étale cover $U_j\to S$ there are finitely presented $A$-modules $N_j$ and isomorphisms $L|_{U_j}\simeq B_{U_j}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{N_j}$. One may choose, for each $j$, finite integers $u_j,v_j$ and a single scalar exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow A^{u_j}\xrightarrow{d_j}A^{v_j}\longrightarrow N_j\longrightarrow0$$
such that its constant sheafification followed by extension to $B_{U_j}$ is exact. For every $n\geq1$, the derived reduction $(L[0]\otimes_B^LB_n)|_{U_j}$ is isomorphic in $D((B_n)_{U_j})$ to
$$[\underline{A_n}^{u_j}\xrightarrow{\overline d_j}\underline{A_n}^{v_j}],$$
in degrees $-1,0$, where $\overline d_j$ is reduction of the same scalar matrix $d_j$. These are isomorphisms of derived objects. They identify the actual quotient-induced transition with the termwise quotient of this matrix complex; hence the identifications hold simultaneously for all $n$ on the same cover. Every scalar ring $A_n$ is finite, including when $\ell$ is ramified in $A$. The two cohomology sheaves are the constant sheaves of $\ker\overline d_j$ and $\operatorname{coker}\overline d_j$, respectively. Both scalar modules are finite as sets and finitely presented over $A_n$. All other cohomology sheaves vanish. Consequently $L[0]\otimes_B^LB_n$ has locally constant finite-type cohomology in degrees $-1,0$. The assertion includes $N_j=0$, $L=0$, and empty $S$; it assumes neither Noetherianity of $S$ nor torsion-freeness of $N_j$.

proof.text: Use the concrete unchanged coefficient and matrix data, publicly reexported from their data module. The ell-power/uniformizer-power cofinality gives a uniformizer-power ideal contained in each ell-power ideal; finite_coefficientExtensionRing and the surjective quotient factor make every actual ell-power residue finite. This covers ramification and exponent zero in the intermediate quotient.

The coefficient integer ring is a PID by extension_integers_dvr; transport the PID and domain structures through ULift.ringEquiv. For each supplied local model use Module.FinitePresentation.exists_fin' to obtain a surjection from finite free scalars. Submodule.basisOfPid gives a finite basis of its kernel. Compose the inverse basis map with kernel inclusion and express it by LinearMap.toMatrix'. Its injectivity and exactness follow from the basis equivalence and the range of kernel inclusion.

Apply the specified scalar-resolution comparison to obtain the completed short exact sequence and all simultaneous derived models. Apply the independent constant-matrix homology computation at every level to get the two slice cohomology identifications.

A reduced kernel is a subtype of a finite power of the finite residue ring. The reduced cokernel is finite by surjectivity of its quotient map. A finite ring is Noetherian and finite modules over it are finitely presented by Module.finitePresentation_of_finite. These are actual Lean proofs, not split-off obligations.

For each V use exactly the covering sieve supplied by the local-model hypothesis. On each arrow choose its scalar model and construct its resolution and simultaneous comparison as above. The matrix homology lemma gives zero restrictions outside -1,0. Sheaf separatedness on that covering sieve proves the identity of the global homology sheaf equals zero: evaluate the identity=zero equation on each zero slice at its identity object and apply it to the restriction of an arbitrary section. Empty covering sieves use the same separatedness axiom. In degrees -1 and 0 use the scalar reduced kernel or cokernel as the local finite module, with the restricted-global homology isomorphism from the matrix calculation.
